why: A is better supported. Both returns pick DVC (c2) and differ only on OpenLineage (c5), which B adds. In catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json, data-dvc (lines 692-735) has decision "default" and a us_equities_fit that pins exact raw/curated snapshots and dependencies. That is the closest retained fit to the requirement for reproducible analytical snapshots. data-openlineage (lines 819-859) has decision "conditional", with the rationale "Useful when several engines need interoperable lineage metadata; keep the initial local pipeline simpler". Its native_workflow only builds a Dataset object and states "no transport or network emission"; it is explicitly UNEXECUTED. Its limitations say it "is not a persistent lineage server, scheduler or dataset version store". B promotes c5 because it matches the scope terms (data-lineage, metadata-events). No retained evidence shows c5 meeting the requirement better than the other conditional source-review candidates (Kafka, MLflow, Iceberg, ArcticDB), and the retained catalog decision itself defers it. So B adds a winner without evidence. A's claims hold up. The DVC workflow is marked unexecuted (line 711). The identity-readiness receipt exists at blueprints/us-equities/identity-readiness/native-receipt.json, and A presents it as separate from DVC acceptance. B's local-code observations also check out: validate_source is at line 68, write_snapshot at 116 with ingested_at from SEC.utc_now() at 135, and per-file sha256 at 138. Since neither set makes a contradicted claim, the only difference is c5, and on that A's set is the better supported. Limitation: I could not open the pinned upstream READMEs from this lane, so the DVC source-review claims rest on the catalog record.
